Those numbers don't just sit there as a flat list. The model needs to figure out *which* tokens are related to *which other* tokens — and that's the job of the **attention mechanism**.

Attention lets the model weigh relationships between tokens, no matter how far apart they are in the sentence.

[EX]In the sentence "The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired" — what does "it" refer to? The animal, not the street. Attention figures this out by scoring how strongly each token connects to every other token, then using those scores to build meaning.[/EX]

This is why context matters so much. The token for "bank" gets interpreted differently in "river bank" vs. "bank account" because attention pulls in the surrounding tokens and shifts the meaning.

Without attention, the model would treat every token in isolation — like reading a sentence one word at a time with no memory of what came before.

[KEY]Attention lets the model connect distant tokens and resolve ambiguity by weighing relationships across the whole prompt.[/KEY]
